title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The image is extremely faint. It looks like a pressure or ghost impression rather than a fresh text. Read directly, its content coincides almost line for line with what the machine transcription assigns to the PREVIOUS page (103): a crossed-out first diagram, then a clean diagram, the remark on horizontal arrows, the fundamental-groupoid diagram, and the formulas P_{G,C} = ∏ P_{G,a}, etc. Either page 104 is an imprint of page 103, or the transcriptions are shifted by one page. In both cases the mathematics is as follows.

Setting. G is a Mumford–Deligne (MD) graph, i.e. the dual graph of a stable pointed curve. Notation:
- A = A(G) is its set of edges (the nodes of the curve).
- I is the set of marked points.
- Â = I ⊔ A.
- M_G is the stratum of curves of type G in the compactified moduli space of curves M̄_{g,ν}.
- For J ⊂ Â, P_{G,J} → M_G is the G_m^J-torsor of 'tangential data' at the elements of J. For a node a, this is the punctured line T_x ⊗ T_y (the smoothing parameter t_a, i.e. the punctured normal direction of the boundary divisor at a). For a marked point i, it is a nonzero tangent vector at i.
- Hence SP_G = P_{G,Â} (all data), P_G = P_{G,A}, SRP_G = P_{G,I}, and RP_G = P_{G,∅} = M_G.

The diagrams. Take a 'generalisation' homomorphism of MD graphs G → G' ≅ G/C, contracting a subset C ⊂ A of edges (smoothing those nodes). Let G^♮ be the fully contracted graph, i.e. smooth curves. One then has a ladder of spaces:
- top row: SP_G → SP_{G'} → SP_{G^♮};
- middle row: P_G → P_{G'} → P_{G^♮} = M_{G^♮};
- lower row: P_{G,C} → RP_{G'} = M_{G'};
- bottom: RP_G = M_G.
The vertical arrows are torus torsors G_m^I, G_m^{A'} (with A' = A \ C = A(G')) and G_m^C, and the squares are cartesian.

The torsor P_G is identified, up to homotopy, with M_{G,G^♮}: a punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum M_G inside the open stratum. Likewise P_{G,C} ≃ M_{G,G'}.

The horizontal maps exist only in the topological category. They come from plumbing: the next page builds curves of type G' from curves of type G by removing disjoint holomorphic discs and gluing along boundary U(1)-torsors. These maps commute with the operator groups G_m^I, G_m^{A'}, and G_m^{Â'} = G_m^I × G_m^{A'}.

Groupoids. Passing to fundamental groupoids gives the analogous ladder of Teichmüller groupoids S𝒯_G, 𝒯_G, 𝒯_{G,C} and R𝒯_G. These are linked by cartesian Z^I, Z^{A'} and Z^C extensions (Dehn twists around nodes and punctures), and the horizontal functors commute with the Z-actions.

Purpose. This is the topological backbone of the 'tour de Teichmüller' of the Esquisse d'un programme. Each boundary stratum yields a 'tangential' Teichmüller groupoid together with gluing functors toward the generic stratum. That is exactly the data needed to define base points at infinity and the maps between lower-dimensional groupoids (the 'Lego' pieces).
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The torus ranks are consistent: P_G → P_{G,C} is a G_m^{A\C} = G_m^{A'}-torsor, matching A(G/C) = A \ C.

The identifications P_G ≃ M_{G,G^♮} and P_{G,C} ≃ M_{G,G'} hold only up to homotopy (deleted tubular neighbourhood versus normal torus bundle). Grothendieck signals this himself: the horizontal maps are defined only topologically and depend on contractible choices.
The machine transcription is largely spurious: it invents can^#, can^♭, π^#, π^♭, Γ_G and \overline{M}. The faint image actually shows the page-103 diagrams.

ideas.what: Torus torsors P_{G,J} of tangential/smoothing data over boundary strata of M̄_{g,ν}, indexed by subsets J of nodes ∪ marked points, with cartesian squares between them
ideas.modern_name: Punctured normal bundles of boundary strata / tangential base points at infinity; framed moduli spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura (1997); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego–Teichmüller game)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) speaks of the Teichmüller tower and base points 'at infinity' only informally

ideas.what: Topological gluing (plumbing) maps P_G → P_{G'} for generalisations G → G/C, commuting with the torus actions, and the induced functors between Teichmüller groupoids compatible with Dehn-twist Z^A-actions
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing/gluing maps; the modular operad structure on (framed) moduli spaces and Teichmüller groupoids

ideas.what: The groupoid ladder S𝒯_G → 𝒯_G → R𝒯_G as cartesian Z^I, Z^A extensions (twists around punctures and nodes)
ideas.modern_name: Central extensions of (stratum) mapping class groupoids by Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in mapping class group theory (Birman, Harvey); framed version in Bakalov–Kirillov

missed.claim: Explicit, systematic pre-1984 construction of the Teichmüller tower's 'tangential' groupoids attached to every boundary stratum, with torus-torsor bookkeeping P_{G,J} (J ⊂ I ⊔ A) and plumbing functors for every generalisation G → G/C. This predates Deligne's tangential base points and the Ihara–Nakamura formalisation. It is documentation of priority/approach rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: Les flèches horizontales ne sont définies que dans la catégorie topologique. Elles commutent aux opérations des groupes d'opérateurs G_m^I resp. G_m^{A'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows that Grothendieck had the full stratified framework, with plumbing functors compatible with Dehn twists, in hand around 1978–81. This bears on the historical attribution of the Teichmüller-tower/Lego formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an essentially duplicate (faint imprint) of page 103. The content is a careful but now standard setup, matching Ihara–Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps and Bakalov–Kirillov. Its interest is mainly as early unpublished evidence of the framework.
transcription_corrections: The page image is a faint ghost impression whose content matches the transcription given for page 103, not the transcription given here.
There are no 'can^#', 'can^♭', 'π^#', 'π^♭' labels. The vertical arrows are torus torsors G_m^I, G_m^{A'}, G_m^C (and Z^I, Z^{A'}, Z^C for the groupoids), marked 'cart'.
The groupoids are S𝒯_G, 𝒯_G, 𝒯_{G,C}, R𝒯_G (Teichmüller groupoids), not SΓ_G, Γ_G, \overline{Γ}_G.
'\overline{M}P_{G''}' should read 'P_{G^♮} = RP_{G^♮} (= M_{G^♮})'. G'' is G^♮.

The bottom-row formulas read P_{G,C} = ∏_{a∈C} P_{G,a}, 𝒯_{G,C} = Π_1 P_{G,C}, SP_G = P_{G,Â}, RP_G = P_{G,∅}, SRP_G = P_{G,I}, with the cartesian square SRP_G ← SP_G over RP_G ← P_G (G_m^A horizontally, G_m^I vertically).
The upper-right annotation reads approximately '[G → G'] homom. de généralisation de graphes MD', with G' ≅ G/C written below.
